statuses.supported: Available through a shared Android/iOS React Native contract.
statuses.partial: Available with a reduced contract or platform differences.
statuses.unsupported: Available in at least one native SDK but not exposed by the wrapper.
statuses.blocked: A safe shared bridge requires additional public native SDK APIs.
statuses.platform-only: Intentionally available on one applicable platform only.

capabilities.area: Captions, quality, and audio through native UI
capabilities.notes: Native pickers cover captions/quality/audio. Programmatic quality selection is bridged on Android via setVideoQuality (Media3 track selection on the public currentPlayer); iOS programmatic quality is not bridged.

Native controls work. RN adds: onPlayerTypeChange event (Android-only cast handover, 'default'/'cast') and enterPiP() command (Android-only; requires android:supportsPictureInPicture="true" on the host activity). Programmatic cast start/stop, AirPlay state, and fullscreen commands are not exposed by either SDK's public API.
No equivalent shared public native API.
Not exposed as a programmatic React Native contract.

Android uses the native SDK PlaybackPositionManager (resumeConfig prop + onResumePositionAvailable event). iOS uses a JS-side fallback (useResumePosition hook with AsyncStorage). Platform persistence differs.
JS-side implementation via seekTo + position tracking. Configurable offset (default 10s).
Android: onChaptersUpdated/onMomentsUpdated events from native player. iOS: fetch via API client (getVideo). Player-view events not available.
Android: onRetentionGraphUpdated event from native player. iOS: fetch via API client (getVideoHeatmap). Player-view event not available.

Platform-agnostic JS API (getAllResumePositions, clearResumePosition, clearAllResumePositions, exportResumePositions, importResumePositions, cleanupExpiredResumePositions). Android delegates to the native PlaybackPositionManager via TurboModule; iOS runs against the pluggable AsyncStorage used by useResumePosition. Export uses the normalized PlaybackPosition JSON shape on both platforms.

getPlaybackSpeeds() queries the native engine on Android (allowedSpeeds → dashboard playerSettings → SDK defaults). iOS has no public speed API — returns the SDK's hardcoded list [0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0].
List, get, play data, create, update, and delete.
List, get, play data, lifecycle, create, update, and delete.
List, get, create, rename, and delete collections with optional preview images.

capabilities.area: Video statistics, heatmap, resolution, and storage API
capabilities.notes: Heatmap, statistics, resolutions, heatmap play data, and detailed storage size are bridged on Android. iOS lacks the play/heatmap and /storage endpoints in the generated client; heatmap, statistics, and resolutions remain shared.
Ingest status and remote, local, listed, and deleted thumbnails are supported.

setThumbnail (remote URL), fetchNewVideo, addCaption, and deleteCaption are shared. uploadThumbnail is Android-only (iOS OpenAPI client has no VOD file-upload endpoint). refetchVideo is Android-native; iOS falls back to getVideo.
reencodeVideo, reencodeUsingCodec (h264/vp9/hevc/av1), repackageVideo, and deleteResolutions (with dryRun) are shared. deleteAllResolutions flag is Android-only.
transcribeVideo is shared (generateChapters/generateMoments are Android-only). smartGenerate is Android-only; iOS OpenAPI client does not expose this operation.
Pause/resume works on iOS (URLSessionTask); no-op on Android basic uploader. Does not survive process death on either platform.

Pause/resume/cancel work on both platforms. iOS TUS survives process death via background URLSession; Android TUS does not (no foreground service). continueUpload resumes on Android; iOS re-issues uploadVideo with the same videoId.

Fabric component backed by native capture pipelines. New VOD recording and existing live stream sources are supported. Camera and microphone permissions must be requested by the host app before mounting.

stopBroadcast, switchCamera, setMuted, and toggleMute are shared. startBroadcast is supported natively on iOS. On Android the public SDK has no start method; the bridge simulates the built-in start button when hideDefaultControls is false, and resolves with an InvalidState error when controls are hidden (TODO(Android SDK): expose a public start method).

iOS maps the quality prop to BroadcastQuality (resolution, frameRate, videoBitrate, audioBitrate). Android hard-codes 1080p30 (~9.3 Mbps video, 64 kbps audio); the quality prop is accepted but ignored.

State (idle/preparing/live), elapsed time, camera position, mute state, ingest endpoint state (primary/backup, connecting/live/offline), reconnecting, reconnect failed, failover, and terminal error events are shared.

Both platforms retry with 1/2/4/8/8s backoff up to 5 attempts, alternating primary and backup ingest. Proactive failover after two consecutive not-live polls. dualPublish publishes to both endpoints simultaneously with independent 5s reconnect on Android.
Neither native SDK exposes a public background-broadcast or interruption-resume API. The broadcaster is foreground-only; host apps must stop the broadcast on app backgrounding.

BunnyImage component and bunnyImageSource() helper inject the Referer header into the platform image pipeline (Fresco/RCTImageLoader) — native cache, no base64. The deprecated useBunnyImage hook remains for compatibility.

useNativeTvPlayer prop (Android-only) routes through the SDK's playVideoWithTVDetection — launches the TV activity when the consumer app also depends on the net.bunny:tv artifact, falls back to the embedded player otherwise. isRunningOnTV() reports leanback support. The iOS SDK does not support tvOS.
Android resolves net.bunny:*:4.0.0 from Maven Central. iOS still uses a pinned local checkout pending a public release tag.
